headword: {不戦条約|ふせんじょうやく}

definitions.gloss: non-aggression pact; anti-war treaty; treaty renouncing war
definitions.explanation: A treaty in which signatory nations agree not to use war as an instrument of national policy. Most commonly refers to the Kellogg-Briand Pact of 1928.

examples.japanese: {不戦条約|ふせんじょうやく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{署名|しょめい}する→署名する：22432_shomeisuru⟧。
{不戦条約|ふせんじょうやく}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{戦争|せんそう}→戦争：01450_sensou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{放棄|ほうき}→放棄：12825_houki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{定|さだ}めた→定める：10448_sadameru⟧⟦{条約|じょうやく}→条約：04912_jouyaku⟧だ。
examples.english: A non-aggression pact is a treaty that stipulates the renunciation of war.

examples.japanese: {千九百二十八年|せんきゅうひゃくにじゅうはちねん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{不戦条約|ふせんじょうやく}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{多|おお}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{国|くに}→国：02204_kuni⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{参加|さんか}した→参加する：25408_sankasuru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦その{後|ご}→その後：08501_sonogo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{第二次世界大戦|だいにじせかいたいせん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{防|ふせ}ぐ→防ぐ：02409_fusegu⟧こと⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦できなかった→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: Although many countries participated in the 1928 non-aggression pact, it could not prevent the subsequent Second World War.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{不戦|ふせん}→不戦：24628_fusen⟧ (non-war, anti-war) and ⟦{条約|じょうやく}→条約：04912_jouyaku⟧ (treaty). Most commonly refers to the Kellogg-Briand Pact ({ケロッグ・ブリアン条約|けろっぐ・ぶりあんじょうやく}) of 1928, which renounced war as a means of resolving international disputes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {不戦条約|ふせんじょうやく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{締結|ていけつ}→締結：13870_teiketsu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to conclude a non-aggression pact
- {不戦条約|ふせんじょうやく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{違反|いはん}→違反：01824_ihan⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to violate a non-aggression pact
- {不戦条約|ふせんじょうやく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{精神|せいしん}→精神：03377_seishin⟧: the spirit of the non-aggression pact

RELATED WORDS:
- {不可侵条約|ふかしんじょうやく}: non-aggression treaty — similar concept, emphasizing not invading
- {平和条約|へいわじょうやく}: peace treaty — a treaty that ends a war
- {停戦協定|ていせんきょうてい}: ceasefire agreement — a temporary halt to fighting

ETYMOLOGY:
The term appears frequently in Japanese history education, particularly in discussions of the interwar period and Japan's path to the Second World War. It is also connected to {日本国憲法|にほんこくけんぽう}{第九条|だいくじょう} (Article 9 of the Japanese Constitution), which renounces war.
